problem:
The position vector $r(t)$ of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
r(t)=⟨{t}^{3}-4{t}^{2},\,2{t}^{4}-{t}^{2}⟩.
$$

Calculate the components of the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t.$

$a=⟨${{field-1}},{{field-2}}$⟩$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Acceleration Vector of a Particle Given Its Position Vector
examples.problem:
The position vector $\mathbf{r}$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
\mathbf{r} = \langle 4t^2+1, 3t^2-t\rangle.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $\mathbf{a}$.
examples.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector. We can do this by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{2}+1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}-t)⟩ \\  & =⟨8t,\,6t-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6t-1)⟩ \\  & =⟨8,6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩,$ measured in $\text{m}/\text{s},$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ seconds is given by

$$
v=⟨3{t}^{2}+2t-1,-4t+5⟩.
$$

Find the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=1\,\text{s}.$ Do not round the answer.

The magnitude of the acceleration is
{{field-1}}
${\text{m/s}}^{2}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}+2t-1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-4t+5)⟩ \\  & =⟨6t+2,\,-4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration at time $t=1,$ we substitute $t=1$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(1) & =⟨6(1)+2,-4⟩ \\  & =⟨8,-4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute $|a(1)|:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}|a(1)| & =|⟨8,-4⟩| \\  & =\sqrt{{8}^{2}+(-4)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{64+16} \\  & =\sqrt{80} \\  & =4\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the magnitude of the acceleration at time $t=1\,\text{s}$ is $4\sqrt{5}{\text{ m/s}}^{2}.$
